name: Item accuracy
what: Correct / incorrect (dichotomous) on a scored item.
usefulness_tail: The base IRT signal; at the tail, accuracy on very hard items is the primary separator once difficulty is high enough to avoid ceiling.
how_to_collect: Log final response vs key per scored item.
how_much_to_collect: >=8-12 scored items per construct per child near the child's ability for a stable theta; more hard items near the cut.

name: Partial-credit (polytomous) score
what: Graded score for multi-step / multi-part items (0..k).
usefulness_tail: Extracts tail information from a single rich item (a partial-credit item behaves like several dichotomous ones), sharpening theta with fewer items.
how_to_collect: Define ordered scoring categories per item; log category reached.
how_much_to_collect: >=4-6 polytomous items per construct; each contributes more information than one dichotomous item.

name: Response time (total)
what: Milliseconds from item onset to submitted answer.
usefulness_tail: Combined with accuracy it separates fast-accurate (able) from slow-accurate; feeds effort-moderated and joint speed-accuracy models.
how_to_collect: Timestamp item render and submit; store ms.
how_much_to_collect: >=20 RT samples per child for a usable per-child RT distribution; log on every item.

name: First-action latency
what: Milliseconds from item onset to the child's first interaction.
usefulness_tail: Indexes planning/encoding before acting; high-ability reflective solvers often show longer first-action latency with fewer revisions.
how_to_collect: Timestamp first pointer/key/drag event.
how_much_to_collect: Every interactive item; >=15 samples for a stable per-child median.

name: Intra-individual RT variability
what: SD or coefficient of variation of RT across items.
usefulness_tail: Consistency (low variability) tracks ability better than peak speed (worst-performance rule); a strong, less-coachable tail signal.
how_to_collect: Compute SD/CV over the child's RT series (correct trials).
how_much_to_collect: >=20-30 RT samples for a reliable CV; do NOT reward raw speed.

name: Lapse rate
what: Frequency / magnitude of the child's slowest responses (worst-performance).
usefulness_tail: The slowest responses, not the fastest, are most diagnostic of ability; fewer lapses => higher ability.
how_to_collect: Take the slowest quartile/decile of RTs; count lapses beyond a threshold.
how_much_to_collect: >=25 trials so the slow tail of the RT distribution is estimable.

name: Revisions / answer changes
what: Count of answer changes, undos, or re-drags before commit.
usefulness_tail: Distinguishes confident tail performers (few, targeted revisions) from guess-and-check; adds process variance beyond right/wrong.
how_to_collect: Increment a counter on each answer change / undo event.
how_much_to_collect: Every item; interpret relative to item difficulty.

name: Solution path / move sequence
what: Ordered sequence of actions taken to reach the answer.
usefulness_tail: Strategy signature: efficient/novel paths mark strong reasoners; supports evidence-model (Bayes-net) scoring that separates HOW, not just WHETHER.
how_to_collect: Append each action {t, action, state} to an event log per item.
how_much_to_collect: Log fully on constructed/interactive items; needs >=5 such items per construct to characterize strategy.

name: Efficiency vs optimal
what: Moves or time used relative to the optimal solution for the item's difficulty.
usefulness_tail: Near-optimal solving at high difficulty is a clean tail separator; catches able children who are also economical.
how_to_collect: Compare M-PATH length/time to a stored optimal for the item.
how_much_to_collect: >=5 items with known optima per construct.

name: Scaffold / hint usage
what: Count and timing of hints or scaffolds the child invokes.
usefulness_tail: Hint-free solving at difficulty is stronger evidence; dynamic-assessment signal (learning rate) can add incremental tail validity.
how_to_collect: Log each hint request with timestamp and item state.
how_much_to_collect: Every item that offers hints; interpret against difficulty.

name: Persistence / time-on-task
what: Time spent engaging a hard item before solving or giving up.
usefulness_tail: Task commitment (Renzulli) is a construct CogAT misses; persistence on hard items adds non-cognitive tail signal and flags disengagement.
how_to_collect: Time from onset to solve/skip on items above the child's level.
how_much_to_collect: >=6 above-level items per child.

name: Error type
what: Classification of errors: near-miss / systematic / random / motor-slip.
usefulness_tail: Near-misses at high difficulty indicate latent ability just below threshold, refining tail placement; filters motor/attention noise.
how_to_collect: Tag the chosen wrong answer against a distractor taxonomy.
how_much_to_collect: Every incorrect response; needs distractors designed with error meaning.

name: Confidence / wager
what: Elicited confidence rating or points wager on the answer.
usefulness_tail: Metacognitive calibration (accuracy of confidence) adds incremental validity and helps down-weight lucky guesses at the tail.
how_to_collect: Optional quick confidence tap or wager after answering.
how_much_to_collect: On a subset (>=8 items) to avoid burden; not every item.

name: Exploration behavior
what: Number of options sampled / states explored before committing.
usefulness_tail: Systematic exploration vs flailing separates strategic tail solvers; useful in open/interactive items.
how_to_collect: Count distinct states/options visited via M-PATH log.
how_much_to_collect: Interactive items only; >=5 per construct.

name: Progress trajectory
what: Partial progress achieved over a multi-step item over time.
usefulness_tail: Turns one hard item into a curve; the shape (fast-to-plateau vs steady) adds tail resolution beyond final score.
how_to_collect: Snapshot state/score at intervals or per sub-step.
how_much_to_collect: Multi-step items; >=4 per construct.

name: Speed-accuracy tradeoff
what: Joint position on the RT x accuracy plane.
usefulness_tail: Models the child's chosen operating point so speed is only credited when accuracy is held; prevents rewarding impulsive fast-wrong responding.
how_to_collect: Pair M-RT with M-ACC per item; fit per-child SAT.
how_much_to_collect: >=20 items with both signals.

name: Ceiling / max difficulty reached
what: Highest item difficulty answered correctly.
usefulness_tail: Directly probes the tail; adaptive escalation to failure pinpoints the child's edge and is the sharpest single tail statistic.
how_to_collect: Track max b-parameter solved under adaptive escalation.
how_much_to_collect: Requires an item bank extending well above grade level (above-level items).

name: Performance drift (fatigue/engagement)
what: Change in accuracy/RT across the session.
usefulness_tail: Detects disengagement/fatigue that would bias a tail decision; lets scoring discount low-effort late items.
how_to_collect: Regress accuracy/RT on item position within session.
how_much_to_collect: Whole session; needs >=30 items to estimate a slope.

name: Engagement / off-task
what: Idle time, focus loss (blur), and re-engagement latency.
usefulness_tail: Gates all other signals: a tail decision is only valid on engaged responses (supports the 'speed as evidence only when engaged' principle).
how_to_collect: Log window blur/idle timers and time-to-resume.
how_much_to_collect: Continuous background logging across the session.

name: Cross-item consistency
what: Reliability of responses across parallel/equivalent items.
usefulness_tail: Reduces conditional standard error at the cut; inconsistent responders near the cut get more items before a decision.
how_to_collect: Compare responses to matched parallel items (same b, cloned via AIG).
how_much_to_collect: >=3 matched pairs near the child's ability.
